text:
Hey, everyone! It’s year three of my trench breakdowns for Fantasy Points, which means that the NFL preseason is just around the corner. I know the offensive line isn’t the sexiest position group to talk about, but how the big boys up front perform directly affects the rest of the offense. If you’re on the pulse of OL play, you have an advantage for fantasy.

Once again, the “games are won and lost in the trenches” quote came true in the biggest game of the year, as the Seahawks’ pass rush put Drake Maye in a torture chamber in Super Bowl LX. It’s overused and cliché at this point, but as a player, coach, scout, or fan, that quote should always have a spot in the back of your mind.

Before I get to my rankings, I want to quickly recap how I evaluate offensive lines. This process came from my 10 years working in the Cleveland Browns’ personnel department. Keep these factors in mind when making roster decisions.

What makes a good offensive line?

Continuity, Continuity, Continuity — The more a unit plays together, the better the communication and overall quality of play. I value four of five starters returning higher than spending the most money in free agency.

Depth — OL injuries can derail any unit (think Tampa Bay), but having quality replacements can keep a team competitive. You can never have too many linemen, but they have to be capable.

Quality additions — Turnover typically happens every year with OL groups. Adding the right veteran or draft pick could be the missing piece to becoming elite.

Veteran/Youth split — Playing offensive line as a rookie or second-year player is incredibly difficult, so having quality vets can speed up a young player’s development.

Coaching — OL is the most technique-heavy position. Having the right person in charge of the room is crucial. I had first-hand experience with this in Cleveland. We hired Bill Callahan in 2020 after years of questionable coaching, and a good unit became one of the league’s best.

Scheme fit — Can these players fit the schemes we’re trying to run? Coaches and GMs have to ask this question; otherwise, the OL will struggle.

A quality offensive line has to be good in both phases. Pass protection has become incredibly important, but being able to grind out a game on the ground is critical to winning a championship. Good offensive lines often go unnoticed because they’re doing everything right.

Let’s get into the rankings.

Scott DiBenedetto’s 2026 NFL Offensive Line Rankings

* Denotes Rookie

$ Denotes New Acquisition

/ denotes a potential battle or a top backup

1. Denver Broncos – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 2

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Garett Bolles

LG Ben Powers / Kage Casey *

C Luke Wattenberg

RG Quinn Meinerz

RT Mike McGlinchey

The first of my 2025 “Elite” offensive lines is the Broncos. This unit was steadily at the top of the list all season long, and returns all five starters for the third straight year. It’s tough to believe this group won’t be elite again, but there is a “major” change: Davis Webb taking over as OC. Yes, Sean Payton is still the play-caller, but changes in messaging and presentation could be more impactful than expected.

I feel like I could copy and paste what I wrote last year, as all five guys are returning. Garett Bolles and Quinn Meinerz were quietly the best LT and RG duo in the game last year. C Luke Wattenberg was excellent, and RT Mike McGlinchey was well above average in the run game.

The weak link was LG Ben Powers. He clearly struggled in both phases, and it’s no shock that Denver selected Kage Casey in the draft. I’m not sure if Casey, as a fourth-round pick, will usurp Powers, but Payton is already looking ahead.

The Broncos were rolling last year before a freak injury to Bo Nix against Buffalo. That moment likely kept Denver out of Super Bowl 60, but the team is built for another run.

2. Indianapolis Colts – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 7

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Bernhard Raimann / Blake Freeland

LG Quenton Nelson

C Tanor Bortolini

RG Matt Goncalves / Jalen Farmer *

RT Jalen Travis

Don’t sleep on Indianapolis’s offensive line heading into 2026. The Colts were rolling into their Week 11 bye at 8-2, then the wheels came off, and they lost seven straight to end 2025. Their offensive line was the engine that got them those eight wins, as Jonathan Taylor racked up nearly 1,600 yards behind this group. I’m expecting more of the same with four starters returning.

Bernhard Raimann and Quenton Nelson form one of the toughest left sides in the league. Nelson has been elite since year one, and Raimann quickly became a steady force, earning a four-year extension last summer. C Tanor Bortolini was an elite run blocker last year, but will need to step up in protection, and RT Jalen Travis did well filling in for Braden Smith for four games.

The question marks are: will Travis hold up over 17 games, and will RG Matt Goncalves continue to be the weak link? Goncalves wasn’t terrible last season, but was noticeably not as productive as his linemates.

I’m excited about this unit again, as it has been consistently above average to elite for years. There was little turnover this offseason, so the Colts should be solid up front in 2026.

3. Chicago Bears – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 15

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Braxton Jones / Ozzy Trapilo

LG Joe Thuney

C Garrett Bradbury $

RG Jonah Jackson

RT Darnell Wright / Theo Benedet

Ryan Poles and Ben Johnson’s offensive line investments worked nearly to perfection in 2025, as the Bears snuck into the “Elite” tier at the end of the season, despite the revolving door at LT. All but one of the starting group returns for 2026, and Chicago is poised to make another run.

Darnell Wright anchored the right side as one of the best run blockers in the league, and RG Jonah Jackson followed suit with a quality season in the run game. LG Joe Thuney was unshockingly outstanding in protection and grinded out a strong run-blocking campaign. What excites me most about this group is that Braxton Jones’ absence didn’t derail it.

Jones made it through Week 4 before sitting for two weeks and being placed on IR. Theo Benedet and Ozzy Trapilo held firm before Trapilo’s late-season patellar tendon injury. Jones has to rebound in 2026, but the Bears have quality depth behind him.

The biggest change is at center, as Garrett Bradbury was acquired via trade after Drew Dalman retired. Bradbury was below average last year in New England, but should fit into Chicago’s well-established OL. This group should be in the top 10 all season.

4. Tampa Bay Buccaneers – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 3

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Tristan Wirfs

LG Ben Bredeson

C Graham Barton

RG Cody Mauch

RT Luke Goedeke / Justin Skule $

Tampa Bay is another team that brings back all five starters, but I’m not as certain about them as I am about Denver. The Bucs were firmly in my “Elite” tier all of 2024, yet ended 2025 below-average. The injury bug hit Tampa Bay hard up front, so I can give them a bit of a pass, but this unit needs to rebound majorly in 2026.

Tristan Wirfs and Luke Goedeke form one of the best tackle combos in the league. Wirfs was elite despite missing the first three games and Week 17. Goedeke also battled foot issues that put him on IR to start the season. These two must stay healthy. Justin Skule is also a quality depth/insurance signing on the edge.

The interior was much more of a mess, caused by both injuries and poor play. Ben Bredeson was lost to a late-season knee injury, but was majorly struggling in the run game. Graham Barton was flat-out bad in protection all season, and Cody Mauch tore his meniscus in Week 2. The Bucs ultimately have to flush 2025 as a lost year up front, but I have faith that this group will return to form if it can avoid the injury bug.

5. Philadelphia Eagles – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 1

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Jordan Mailata

LG Landon Dickerson

C Cam Jurgens

RG Tyler Steen / Micah Morris *

RT Lane Johnson

I can’t say that 2025 was a banner year for my projected best offensive line. Philadelphia may have gone through a Super Bowl hangover that lasted all season, and ultimately ended with A.J. Brown’s departure. This unit was ultimately a big disappointment, but all five starters return.

Jordan Mailata and Lane Johnson are still arguably the best tackle pair in the game. Johnson is closer to the end of his career, but these two remain a major force. Cam Jurgens and Tyler Steen were fine in their first years starting at C and RG, respectively. Steen was better overall, and Jurgens will have to improve in protection.

The unit’s biggest issue last year was Landon Dickerson. He suffered a meniscus injury in training camp that lingered all season, so he was clearly not the same player, particularly in protection. Jalen Hurts makes life difficult on his line, but Dickerson’s injury didn’t help matters.

If Dickerson returns to full strength, the Eagles should rebound up front. That said, there are a bunch of changes, as longtime OL coach Jeff Stoutland has moved on. Chris Kuper takes over the room, and Sean Mannion comes in as OC. This group is too vet-heavy to let those changes affect it, but don’t be surprised if the Eagles get off to a slow start.

6. Los Angeles Rams – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 9

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Alaric Jackson

LG Steve Avila / Beaux Limmer

C Coleman Shelton

RG Kevin Dotson

RT Warren McClendon Jr. / Keagen Trost *

Assuming this unit has all five projected starters, the Rams are once again poised to be one of the better offensive lines in the league. I left this unit for dead once the injury bug hit early in 2025, but Los Angeles was pushing for “Elite” status by the end of the season.

Veteran RG Kevin Dotson anchors this group and was highly productive last year, despite playing for a stretch with a heavily wrapped hand. RT Warren McClendon was much better than I expected in 2025, which makes me confident the right side will be dangerous. Steve Avila and Coleman Shelton have some things to clean up inside. Shelton, in particular, was replacement level in protection, so watch for Beaux Limmer to see some time if needed.

There’s a big question mark around LT Alaric Jackson. On the field, he was solidly above-average in both phases last year, but he’s facing a domestic violence charge heading into 2026. Jackson was the team’s most consistent blocker last year, so losing him for any stretch would be rough.

The Rams could make a Super Bowl run in 2026, but not if they endure another season with many OL lineup changes due to injuries.

7. Buffalo Bills – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 6

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Dion Dawkins

LG Alec Anderson / Austin Corbett $

C Connor McGovern

RG O’Cyrus Torrence

RT Spencer Brown

The Bills once again have major continuity up front heading into 2026, as four of the five starters return. Joe Brady takes over as head coach, but that shouldn’t be an issue, as he was the offensive coordinator for the last two and a half years. Buffalo’s window is still open, and this is the least amount of change that can happen when a new head coach is hired. But priority No. 1 is keeping Josh Allen upright.

Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown return to anchor the edges. They aren’t on the same level as the pairs in Philadelphia and Tampa Bay, but these two are quietly a top-five duo. O’Cyrus Torrence returns for year four at RG, and Connor McGovern is back after Allen convinced the front office to give his center $52 million.

The only new starter is Alec Anderson at LG, but he’s far from a guy who just walked in off the street. Anderson has been Buffalo’s jumbo TE the last few years, and saw some extended run at LG in 2025. The biggest change up front is the new OL coach, Pat Meyer, replacing Aaron Kromer. This group is so vet-heavy that a new voice shouldn’t drastically alter things, but this unit had a clear problem protecting Allen, and it needs to be fixed quickly.

8. Detroit Lions – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 5

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Penei Sewell

LG Christian Mahogany / Ben Bartch $

C Cade Mays $ / Juice Scruggs $

RG Tate Ratledge

RT Blake Miller * / Larry Borom $

Detroit, like Baltimore, has seen a major shake-up with its offensive line. Just two years ago, the Lions had a top-two OL in football. There was a slight regression last year with essentially the same crew, and now there are major changes with four positions seeing new starters.

LG Christian Mahogany is the only returning starter playing the same position, and 2025 was fairly disastrous, particularly in protection. Tate Ratledge moves to RG in year two. He was adequate as a rookie, but he also needs work in pass pro. The big move is Penei Sewell (finally) moving to LT after Taylor Decker’s release. Sewell is arguably the best tackle in football, regardless of side, so he should be fine on the left.

After those three, five new faces could all see time on the field. Rookie RT Blake Miller replaces Sewell and should be a capable starter. His athletic limitations will keep his ceiling low, but his floor is fairly high, thanks to starting over 50 games at Clemson. Veteran Larry Borom comes in as Miller’s backup. The Lions also added Cade Mays, Juice Scruggs, and Ben Bartch in the interior. Mays is slated to start at center, but don’t be surprised if all three see time this year.

Also, like Baltimore, Detroit is in a new offensive era with Drew Petzing taking over as OC. We’ll have to let Petzing’s system play out, but I’d put a lot of faith in the Lions’ veteran-heavy offense to make plays when it matters. That said, things start up front, and this is the most change that Jared Goff will have had to deal with from his OL since he’s been in Detroit.

9. Los Angeles Chargers – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 10

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Rashawn Slater

LG Jake Slaughter *

C Tyler Biadasz $

RG Cole Strange $ / Kayode Awosika $

RT Joe Alt

Both Los Angeles teams were snake-bitten with offensive line issues last season, but the Chargers definitely “won” that race after losing Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt at different points. With those two healthy and three other changes, Justin Herbert essentially has a brand new offensive line blocking for him.

Slater returns after brutally tearing his patellar tendon during training camp. That should have been a sign of things to come for Los Angeles, as Alt played only six games after suffering multiple ankle injuries. These are the two cornerstones of this unit, so it’s still impressive that the Chargers got to the playoffs without either of them.

The real changes are across the interior as Tyler Biadasz and Cole Strange come over in free agency, and Jake Slaughter comes in as a second-round pick. Biadasz was solid last year, but Strange is a replacement-level player. Slaughter should eventually become the starting center, but he’s more than capable of being a productive guard in year one.

Expect a slow start from this group as all five get used to playing with each other, but the tackles and Biadasz should carry the unit early.

10. Atlanta Falcons – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 12

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Jake Matthews / Wanya Morris $

LG Matthew Bergeron

C Ryan Neuzil

RG Chris Lindstrom

RT Jawaan Taylor $

The Falcons just couldn’t get out of their own way last season. Atlanta had a plethora of talent on both sides of the ball (much of which is returning), but a midseason five-game losing streak sank the year. Kevin Stefanski now takes over as head coach, and his offensive line is built for his wide zone rushing attack.

The ironman Jake Matthews returns at LT. He’s still superb in protection, but his run blocking took a major dip last year. Matthew Bergeron is still getting better heading into year four to complete a quality left side. C Ryan Neuzil and RG Chris Lindstrom round out the returning starters as a pair of elite run blockers who could be better in protection. I’m still high on the returning group for Atlanta, as their play styles mesh extremely well with Stefanski’s system.

However, Jawann Taylor could derail the entire unit. Taylor comes over from Kansas City as a cap casualty after failing as the Chiefs’ big free agent signing a few years ago. He never lived up to the billing in KC and was a replacement-level run blocker last year.

Taylor scares me, but I’ll lean on the rest of the group and quality coaching, as Bill Callahan reconnects with Stefanski. This OL should be in or near the top 10 all season.

11. Carolina Panthers – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 18

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Ikem Ekwonu

LG Damien Lewis

C Luke Fortner $

RG Robert Hunt

RT Taylor Moton / Monroe Freeling *

Carolina’s offensive line has been trending up the last couple of seasons and should push to be a top-half or top 10 unit this year. The Panthers overperformed in 2025 and 2026 will come down to quarterback play, but Bryce Young will have a quality group blocking for him.

Four starters return for Carolina, anchored by Ikem Ekwonu (currently injured) and Taylor Moton at the tackle spots. Moton remains reliable heading into year 10. RG Robert Hunt returns after missing most of 2025 with a torn biceps, and LG Damien Lewis will look to build off an exceptional year in both phases.

The two new faces are Luke Fortner, who comes over from New Orleans to replace Austin Corbett at C, and first-round pick Monroe Freeling. Fortner is on a super cheap deal after an impressive 2025. Freeling should become Moton’s long-term replacement, although he has the build and athleticism to play on either side. He might have to play right away opposite Moton given Ekwonu’s January patellar tendon tear.

With the exception of Ekwonu’s injury problems, things remain bright in Carolina.

12. Dallas Cowboys – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 20

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Tyler Guyton

LG Tyler Smith

C Cooper Beebe / Nick Leverett

RG Tyler Booker

RT Terence Steele / Drew Shelton *

The Cowboys' offensive line overperformed my expectations last year. I didn’t think the group would be awful, but I didn't anticipate it would become a top-10 unit by the end of the season. All five starters are back, so expect a solid season from the boys up front.

LG Tyler Smith is the rock that holds things together in Dallas, and he put in an elite run-blocking season last year. C Cooper Beebe was average or better in both phases, and RG Tyler Booker was an outstanding run blocker as a rookie.

If there are questions, they’re at tackle, as Terence Steele and Tyler Guyton aren’t the best pair. Steele is a strong enough run blocker to survive, but, in my opinion, this is a make-or-break year for Guyton. The continuity should naturally get this group close to the top 10, but I’m still on the fence about the tackle situation.

13. Jacksonville Jaguars – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 21

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Cole Van Lanen / Walker Little

LG Ezra Cleveland / Emmanuel Pregnon *

C Robert Hainsey

RG Patrick Mekari

RT Anton Harrison

Jacksonville should have big expectations for 2026. They fell short against Buffalo in the playoffs, but this team had a lot working for it last year. The offensive line, in particular, should be solid with four-plus starters returning (I’ll clarify). The Jaguars will ultimately go as far as Trevor Lawrence takes them, but he should be comfortable in the pocket.

I’ll say that none of the returning starters were particularly impressive last year in year one of Liam Coen. LG Ezra Cleveland was firmly the best and was the group’s best in protection. C Robert Hainsey struggled in both phases, and RT Anton Harrison was slightly better. My biggest disappointment was with RG Patrick Mekari. He’s my favorite utility lineman, but a full season at one spot apparently wasn’t the best thing.

The big change is that Cole Van Lanen will now start at LT. Van Lanen was excellent in the Mekari-esque utility role, playing both guard and tackle spots in 2025. Will he continue to be solid or crumble playing only one spot?

Be on the lookout for rookie guard Emmanuel Pregnon. The Oregon product is built to be a downhill grinder, so be aware of any run scheme changes if he sees extended time in 2026.

14. Seattle Seahawks – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 30

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Charles Cross

LG Grey Zabel

C Jalen Sundell / Olu Oluwatimi

RG Anthony Bradford / Beau Stephens *

RT Abraham Lucas

Hand up! I missed on Seattle’s offensive line last year, slotting them in at No. 30 heading into 2025. Were they world beaters? No. Seattle was one of the league’s worst rushing teams in the regular season, and Sam Darnold’s quick time to throw (2.52 seconds) saved this unit more often than not. But this group deserved much more credit than I gave it, and the best part is that all five starters return for 2026.

Charles Cross and Abe Lucas anchor the edges. They were solidly above-average in both phases and should carry positive momentum into 2026. Their protection grades will be somewhat inflated, thanks to Darnold and the scheme, but these two are very capable tackles. Grey Zabel will look to build on a fine rookie season, and Jalen Sundell proved that he’s a steady blocker in the middle.

The issue up front for Seattle is RG Anthony Bradford. He shockingly started every game last year despite being one of the worst RGs in the NFL. He particularly struggled in protection. Bradford is entering the final year of his contract, so could we see Olu Oluwatimi or rookie Beau Stephens at RG at any point?

Seattle is coming off a Super Bowl victory, but there are changes on offense as Brian Fluery takes over as OC following Klint Kubiak's departure. The Seahawks are built for another run, but how long will it take to get rolling on offense?

15. Baltimore Ravens – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 4

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Ronnie Stanley

LG Olaivavega Ioane *

C Danny Pinter $ / Jovaughn Gwyn $

RG John Simpson $

RT Roger Rosengarten

I’ve been a Ravens OL supporter for the last couple of seasons, mainly because of continuity and quality coaching. Unfortunately, both are gone in 2026, as only two starters return and Jesse Minter takes over as head coach.

The returners are both tackles, as vet stalwart Ronnie Stanley anchors the edge with young RT Roger Rosengarten. Stanley was still effective in year 10, but I was very impressed with how well Rosengarten did in year two. This is a strong duo that will have to lead the unit. Meanwhile, the interior has been completely reworked after losing Tyler Linderbaum and both guards.

The exciting piece is rookie LG Vega Ioane. Without a doubt, he was the best guard in the draft, and he has the build and mentality to be a road-grating Ravens run blocker. However, I’m less fired up about the other two additions. RG John Simpson returns for his second stint with Baltimore after signing a three-year deal, and C Danny Pinter comes over from Indianapolis on a one-year contract. Neither was particularly strong last season, so expect a slow start from the interior three.

It’s a new era in Baltimore for Lamar Jackson and the rest of the offense. Jackson will make plays, but I have a hard time believing in his offensive line.

16. Arizona Cardinals – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 8

Projected Starting Lineups

LT Paris Johnson

LG Isaac Seumalo $

C Hjalte Froholdt

RG Chase Bisontis *

RT Elijah WIlkinson $ / Oli Udoh $

Man, was I a fan of the Cardinals heading into 2025. The offensive line got me fired up with how it ended 2024, and then the unit had little turnover at the start of last season. This group ultimately finished firmly in my “Average” tier, and now three new faces have stepped in after.

LT Paris Johnson and C Hjalte Froholdt return after steady 2025 campaigns. I have more faith in Johnson to carry over his performance, as Froholdt is dealing with two new guards on either side of him. Vets Isaac Seumalo and Elijah Wilkinson come over from Pittsburgh and Atlanta, respectively. Seumalo was excellent in protection last year, while Wilkinson will need to be better in both phases.

The big addition is RG Chase Bisontis. The 34th overall pick was one of my favorite interior linemen in the draft, and I would have been very comfortable spending a first-round pick on him. He’s strong, quick, and athletic enough for both rushing schemes and should be starting for the next decade.

I’m not expecting much from Arizona’s offense this year with the quarterback issues, but the offensive line should be a top-half unit.

17. Minnesota Vikings – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 14

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Christian Darrisaw / Caleb Tiernan *

LG Donovan Jackson

C Blake Brandel

RG Will Fries

RT Brian O’Neill / Ryan Van Demark $

Minnesota is another group I expected more from last season, but the OL could never put it all together. There’s one big change and a couple other new faces up front. Oh, and there’s (most likely) a new quarterback in Kyler Murray.

The good news is that Christian Darrisaw, Donovan Jackson, Will Fries, and Brian O’Neill are all back. Yes, I typically favor continuity, but it’s nuanced with Minnesota. O’Neill was the best of the group in both phases, but Darrisaw never fully recovered from his major knee injury in 2024 and played only 10 games. Jackson was better than expected in protection as a rookie, but Fries was consistently below-average in 2024. Blake Brandel takes over at C for Ryan Kelly, after splitting time between C and LG last year.

There’s a ton of continuity with the group, but the front office signed Ryan Van Demark from Buffalo and drafted Caleb Tiernan in the third round. These feel like insurance moves, and that the powers that be don’t fully trust the unit. The Vikings will compete in the NFC North, but I don’t see Murray getting this group to the postseason.

18. San Francisco 49ers – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 16

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Trent Williams

LG Connor Colby / Carver Willis *

C Jake Brendel / Brett Toth $

RG Dominick Puni

RT Colton McKivitz

2025 was a roller coaster for the 49ers. After enduring a season from hell in 2024, San Francisco was a win away from home-field advantage in the playoffs, but lost at home to Seattle in Week 18, then again on the road in the Divisional Round. The offensive line was the backbone of Kyle Shanahan’s offense, but the unit majorly regressed last season.

Future Hall of Famer Trent Williams is back at LT, and was once again elite in year 16 (!!!). RT Kolton McKivitz carried his weight on the other side, completing one of the best tackle duos in the game. However, the interior left much to be desired last season.

RG Dominick Puni and C Jake Brendel weren’t atrocious, but were far from good in both phases, and then rookie Connor Colby was awful in protection, filling in for Ben Bartch. Bartch is gone, so Colby is slated to start at LG, but don’t be shocked if free agent signing Brett Toth or fourth-round pick Carver Willis see time.

San Francisco still has continuity up front and quality coaching to be competitive in the NFC West. I think LG will be a problem and could be a revolving door all season, but I expect the group to rebound in 2026.

19. New England Patriots – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 23

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Will Campbell

LG Alijah Vera-Tucker $

C Jared Wilson

RG Mike Onwenu

RT Morgan Moses / Caleb Lomu *

Have the Patriots been in the headlines for anything this offseason?

After making a surprise run to the Super Bowl, New England turns over two spots on the offensive line that struggled to protect Drake Maye against Seattle. Maye was partially to blame, but this unit had trouble keeping him clean all season, and finished with a modest 4.44 YPC (14th). New England has taken a couple of big swings with the two additions in hopes of making life easier on Maye.

Starting with the returners, LT Will Campbell faded down the stretch and was the focal point of abuse in the playoffs, thanks to a Week 12 knee injury (or because of his short arms?). 2025 was a solid rookie year overall, but he’ll have much to prove that his playoff performance was a fluke. RG Mike Onwenu continued to be a high-level producer, and RT Morgan Moses was solid in year 12, particularly in the run game.

New England made two key additions this offseason. The first is rookie tackle Caleb Lomu. The “other” Utah tackle will back up either Campbell or Moses, and could be the long-term option opposite Campbell. He’s another big, athletic tackle, but isn’t ready to see the field. The other move was signing Alijah Vera-Tucker away from the Jets. He didn’t play at all last season after tearing his triceps prior to Week 1. He was a firmly above-average performer in 2024 and is an instant upgrade from Cole Strange.

I like the moves New England made, but priority No. 1 has to be keeping Maye upright. Maye himself has to improve his awareness when under pressure, but the Patriots have given him a lot to work with up front.

20. New Orleans Saints - 2025 Preseason Ranking: 25

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Kelvin Banks Jr.

LG David Edwards $

C Erik McCoy

RG Cesar Ruiz / Jeremiah Wright *

RT Taliese Fuaga

The Saints’ offensive line is well-suited for a step forward in 2025. That’s not a super-high bar, as they were firmly in my “Yikes” tier at the end of last season. But it’s hard to deny how well the offense played overall down the stretch. Tyler Shough is the man in New Orleans, and year two of Kellen Moore’s offense gives me hope.

It’s no surprise that New Orleans couldn’t run the ball in 2025 (31st in YPC, 3.69), but it wasn’t the fault of LT Kelvin Banks. There were questions about Banks as a rookie, but he became the team’s most effective run blocker last year, and he was more than serviceable in protection. Unfortunately, that’s where the firm positives stop for the Saints.

All of the other three returning starters were below-average in the run game (well below for RG Cesar Ruiz), and I was most disappointed with RT Taliese Fuaga. I expected a bigger jump in year two, but I can chalk it up to it being the first year in a new system if he comes out strong in 2026. The big addition is LG David Edwards, who comes over from Buffalo. New Orleans gave him a four-year deal, and he’s an instant run game upgrade.

It would be a major disappointment if there isn’t a clear effort to improve the run game in 2026, and Edwards’ arrival creates a solid run blocking left side. I don’t think this unit will finish the season in the top half, but there should be a clear step forward.

21. Green Bay Packers – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 13

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Jordan Morgan

LG Aaron Banks

C Sean Rhyan

RG Anthony Belton / Jager Burton *

RT Zach Tom

I’ll be honest, I haven’t been able to make much sense of Green Bay’s offensive line the last couple of years. They’re consistently good enough to be around the middle, but the unit hasn’t taken a collective step forward. That said, the Packers are another team where all five projected starters saw time last year, just in a different alignment.

The most consistent performer last season was RT Zach Tom. He was solid in both phases and will have to again in 2026. Jordan Morgan will slide over to LT full time (hopefully) after playing everywhere but center last season. Aaron Banks returns at LG after a subpar season, but the real problems for Green Bay are at RG and C.

Sean Rhyan and Anthony Belton played multiple positions last season … but did so at well below replacement level in both phases. Jager Burton comes in as a fifth-round pick, but I wouldn’t be shocked if he saw some time along the interior. I’m interested to see how much losing Elgton Jenkins affects the group.

I want to like this unit more, and the Packers will be in the mix thanks to Jordan Love, but the offensive line needs to prove it to me. By the numbers, last year wasn’t pretty, as the group finished in my “Bad” tier. Can they rebound?

22. Miami Dolphins – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 28

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Patrick Paul / Jamaree Salyer $

LG Kadyn Proctor *

C Aaron Brewer

RG Jonah Savaiinaea

RT Austin Jackson / Charlie Heck $

For the mess that was the 2025 Miami Dolphins, the offensive line wasn’t as big an issue as I thought it would be. It wasn’t better than average, but the unit held things together well enough to produce the fourth-best YPC in the league (4.73). However, there’s plenty of work to be done for new head coach Jeff Hafley and offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik.

The good news is that four starters return for Miami. LT Patrick Paul performed better than expected in both phases, RT Austin Jackson was fine returning from injury, and C Aaron Brewer was one of the best centers in football. That said, RG Jonah Savaiinaea was a huge weak link, particularly in protection. He moves over to the right side after being arguably the worst LG in the NFL in 2025.

His replacement at LG is first-round pick Kadyn Proctor. I was a big fan of the Alabama product in the lead-up to the draft. He’s a freakishly athletic dude for his size, has the strength to grind down defenders, and can kick outside if needed. He certainly needs to refine some aspects of his game, but Miami got a steal with Proctor at No. 12.

I need to see it before I believe that Miami’s offensive line will pick up Slowik’s system, but this group overachieved last year, has a lot of continuity, and adds a solid rookie to the mix.

23. Washington Commanders – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 11

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Laremy Tunsil / Brandon Coleman

LG Chris Paul / Timothy McKay

C Nick Allegretti

RG Sam Cosmi / Andrew Wylie

RT Josh Conerly Jr.

Talk about a flop. I had the Commanders' OL pushing the top 10 heading into last year, after an impressive 2024 campaign. But Jayden Daniels’ injury magnified an entire team regression, and the unit finished with a large split between run and pass performance. There are multiple moving parts up front, but the silver lining is that everyone was on the team last year.

Laremy Tunsil continues to be a force on the edge and must be the anchor of this unit in 2026. Josh Conerly was serviceable as a rookie, but there’s a lot of work to be done in both phases. The interior is where the movement is, as Nick Allegretti replaces Tyler Biadasz at center, and Sam Cosmi returns after an injury-riddled 2025. Cosmi was good in the games he played, but will he return to form?

Chris Paul is also back at LG, but he had arguably the biggest split between pass pro and run blocking. It’s frankly surprising the Commanders averaged the fifth-best YPC (4.73) despite having one of the worst run-blocking left guards.

It’s not a secret that 2026 is important for many within the Commanders’ organization. I think this unit and the offense as a whole bounce back, but it will be a battle for Washington to make the playoffs.

24. Kansas City Chiefs – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 19

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Josh Simmons / Esa Pole

LG Kingsley Suamataia

C Creed Humphrey

RG Trey Smith

RT Jaylon Moore / Kahlil Benson *

Was 2025 a blip or the new way of things for Kansas City? The Chiefs were a bottom-half rushing team and one of the worst in protection last year, yet they return four full-time starters.

C Creed Humphrey and RG Trey Smith anchor the unit, with Humphrey being the best center in the league last year, and LG Kingsley Suamataia was serviceable in his first year as a starter. LT Josh Simmons had an interesting run-pass split as a rookie, performing much better-than-expected in protection. Can he build on it?

The major change is at RT, as the Jawaan Taylor experiment officially failed. Jaylon Moore saw time at both tackle spots last year, and was flat-out bad in protection. Esa Pole and rookie free agent Kahlil Benson are the reserve tackles, so Moore should get a bit of a leash this year.

25. Pittsburgh Steelers – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 29

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Troy Fautanu / Broderick Jones

LG Mason McCormick / Gennings Dunker *

C Zach Frazier

RG Spencer Anderson / Brock Hoffman $

RT Dylan Cook / Max Iheanachor *

Much like with Houston, I wasn’t a huge fan of Pittsburgh’s offensive line heading into last season. There was a lot of youth to get excited about, but the overall unit somewhat flopped in Aaron Rodgers’ first year as a Steeler. Mike McCarthy (huh???) takes over as head coach, so there’s hope that he and Rodgers can get the spark back for one more season.

Zach Frazier and Mason McCormick anchor the unit as one of the best center-guard pairs in the league. These two came to Pittsburgh together in the 2024 draft and have been above-average each of the last two seasons. McCormick is moving to the left side this year. Troy Fautanu also came to the Steelers in 2024 and was fine on the right side last season. He’s bumped Broderick Jones out at LT, so the Steelers believe he can get the job done, but I expected a bigger step forward last year.

The questions are with RG Spencer Anderson and RT Dylan Cook. Each saw some playing time in 2025, but neither was in a starting role. Expect both to be in preseason battles with free agent Brock Hoffman and 2026 draft pick Gennings Dunker. Dunker will start his career at guard, but he played tackle at Iowa and has the right mentality for a Steelers lineman. The wild card is first-round pick Max Iheanachor. I really liked how much he improved over the course of last season at Arizona State, but there’s still a lot of rawness to his game. The plan could be to redshirt Iheanachor in 2026, but I wouldn’t be surprised if he saw some time this year.

Pittsburgh has a lot to work with up front. Everyone is young and talented, but will the group struggle to handle the Rodgers-McCarthy dynamic? I expect a better overall season from this unit, but there will likely be hiccups.

26. Cincinnati Bengals – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 27

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Orlando Brown, Jr.

LG Dylan Fairchild / Brian Parker II *

C Ted Karras / Connor Lew *

RG Dalton Risner

RT Amarius Mims

Cincinnati’s offensive line had a forgettable 2025. The unit was awful in pass protection and below average in run blocking. The Bengals were snake-bit by their defense, but the offensive line was a close second as the team’s worst unit. It’s shocking to me that there weren’t more changes up front this offseason. How hot is Zac Taylor’s seat?

The silver lining is that there’s plenty of experience and continuity for this group. Orlando Brown, Ted Karras, and Dalton Risner each have at least seven years of experience, and Risner was more than capable as a late-training-camp addition. That said, Risner was the best of the three last year, as Brown and Karras underperformed.

The youth elements of Cincinnati’s OL are LG Dylan Fairchild and RT Amarius Mims. I’m a fan of Mims and how athletic he is for his size, but both need to take another step forward in 2026, particularly in the run game. I also like what Cincinnati did in the draft, bringing in Connor Lew and Brian Parker II. Lew was my favorite center, and Parker should be a quality depth piece early in his career. I’d expect Parker to see time first, but both could get on the field this season.

If the Bengals get average offensive line play, Joe Burrow will take care of the rest, but this unit needs to be significantly better in 2026.

27. Tennessee Titans - 2025 Preseason Ranking: 24

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Dan Moore Jr.

LG Pete Skoronski / Fernando Carmona *

C Austin Schlottmann $ / Pat Coogan *

RG Cordell Volson $

RT J.C. Latham

A lot has changed in Tennessee since I wrote this article last year. Brian Callahan is out, and Robert Saleh is a head coach again. Along with Saleh comes Brian Daboll, the new offensive coordinator, and a new offensive mentality for the Titans. By the numbers, Tennessee’s OL wasn’t terrible in 2025, but how much will Daboll’s scheme improve the new-look unit in 2026?

The returners are LT Dan Moore, LG Pete Skoronski, and RT J.C. Latham. Skoronski was clearly the best of the group in both phases, with Latham adding quality to the run game and Moore being capable, albeit not outstanding. These three will have to be solid for Cam Ward as they, along with the two new starters, learn Daboll’s system.

The new guys are C Austin Schlottmann and RG Cordell Volson, who come over from the Giants and Bengals, respectively. Schlottmann put together a quality season on limited reps in both phases for New York, but Volson is coming off a preseason shoulder injury and didn’t play at all in 2025.

There are a lot of moving parts for Ward to get used to, and he’ll have to rely on his offensive line picking things up quickly. I think this unit ends up in the middle of the pack, but Daboll should make the Titans more exciting to watch on offense.

28. New York Jets - 2025 Preseason Ranking: 26

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Olu Fashanu

LG Dylan Parham $

C Josh Myers

RG Joe Tippmann

RT Armand Membou / Chukwuma Okorafor

Ah, the Jets. It feels like 2026 will end in disaster and Aaron Glenn being fired. The vibes aren’t great for Gang Green, and the offense starts fresh with Frank Reich coming on as OC and Geno Smith returning. I don’t think things will go well overall, but there are some positives up front.

Starting with the 2025 bright spots, RT Armand Membou stepped in and performed very well as a rookie. There were early bumps, but he cleaned up his game and became the best of this bunch. Joe Tippmann was also solid in 2025 and moved to RG after earning a big four-year extension this offseason. Steady free agent Dylan Parham comes over from Las Vegas at LG.

As for the question marks, LT Olu Fashanu hasn’t lived up to his first-round pedigree yet. There’s still time for the young tackle, but he really struggled in the run game last year. C Josh Myers returns and should probably be up for replacement after below-average performances in both phases in 2025.

Seemingly like always, the Jets have a lot of moving pieces up front and a new quarterback under center. This offense needs to find an identity and stick to it. New York could run the ball last year (8th in YPC, 4.60), but was one of the worst in protection. That was partially quarterback-driven, but something needs to be figured out up front quickly enough to save the head coach’s job.

29. New York Giants – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 31

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Andrew Thomas

LG Jon Runyan

C John Michael Schmitz / Patrick Lucas $

RG Francis Mauigoa * / Daniel Faalele $

RT Jermaine Eluemunor

There was a lot for Giants fans to get excited about last season as Jaxson Dart and Cam Skattebo were the coolest pair of New York bros for a hot minute. The duo didn’t make it through 2025, as Skattebo tried to walk off a nasty ankle injury and Dart dealt with concussion issues. That said, there’s hope again in the Meadowlands, as John Harbaugh takes over, and the Giants may have figured something out up front.

I preach continuity, and the Giants have a ton of it with four starters coming back. Pro’s pro LT Andrew Thomas still anchors the unit, which sees rookie Francis Mauigoa slide in at RG. I was a big fan of Mauigoa, as he has the size and strength to grind things out in the run game, and had much better-than-expected foot speed in protection. New York even added quality veteran depth with Patrick Lucas and Daniel Faalele. There are pieces to work with here.

However, the other three returning starters aren’t the best in the business. RT Jermaine Eluemunor re-signed after having a major split between protection and run blocking. Meanwhile, C John Michael Schmitz and LG Jon Runyan were below-average in both phases. There’s work to be done for Harbaugh and new OC Matt Nagy, but I’m expecting a slight rise from this unit overall.

30. Houston Texans – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 32

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Aireontae Ersery

LG Wyatt Teller $ / Evan Brown $

C Keylan Rutledge * / Jake Andrews

RG Ed Ingram / Febechi Nwaiwu *

RT Braden Smith $ / Trent Brown

It was no secret that I wasn’t a fan of Houston’s offensive line heading into 2025. The unit directly contributed to C.J. Stroud’s year two regression, and things seemed to be heading down a similar path last season. The Texans struggled to run the ball all year (3.90 YPC), but this group surprised me by finishing middle-of-the-road in protection. Will year two of Nick Caley’s offense be different?

The two returning starters are LT Aireontae Ersery and RG Ed Ingram. Ersery is on the way up after gaining a ton of experience as a rookie, and Ingram wound up starting 14 games. Ingram was much better as a run blocker than in protection. These two should form some sense of stability for Stroud. However, the Texans are once again hoping that a major shakeup will create lasting success with three new starters in 2026.

Rookie C Keylan Rutledge is slated to start, but don’t be surprised if veteran Jake Andrews sees time. Braden Smith (Colts), Wyatt Teller (Browns), and Evan Brown (Cardinals) all come over in free agency and will be in position battles at RT (Smith and Trent Brown) and RG, respectively. Stroud is once again in a tough situation, as yet again he’ll have to get comfortable with a shaken-up offensive line. Houston picked up his fifth-year option, but I think it’s “put up or shut up” for Stroud this season, despite the new-look OL. 2026 feels like another season of the Texans relying on the defense.

31. Las Vegas Raiders – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 22

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Kolton Miller

LG Spencer Burford $

C Tyler Linderbaum $

RG Jackson Powers-Johnson / Caleb Rodgers

RT D.J. Glaze

Las Vegas’ offensive line was arguably the biggest disappointment in the league last season. I didn’t think they’d be excellent, but Ashton Jeanty was a shell of himself as a rookie, and the unit produced the worst YPC in the NFL (3.57). Moves had to be made up front, and the Raiders did that by adding Tyler Linderbaum and (to a lesser extent) Spencer Burford. How well will Klint Kubiak’s Super Bowl-winning offense translate to Las Vegas?

LT Kolton Miller is slated to return after missing most of last year with an ankle injury. He was on track for an excellent season in both phases in year eight. Jackson Powers-Johnson is also returning from a season-ending ankle injury, but wasn’t doing as well as Miller. All-name team D.J. Glaze also returns at RT after a subpar 2025.

There was clearly a lot of room to improve for this unit, and giving Linderbaum $81 million over three years should prove that. He had a fairly large run-pass split last season, but this will be a quality move for the Raiders. That said, the Burford signing feels like Vegas was stuck wanting a vet but didn't have the money, as the former 49er ranked near the bottom in protection last season.

Linderbaum signals that Vegas is ready to invest in its new quarterback. Fernando Mendoza will have enough to deal with as a rookie once he eventually plays, and giving him a quality center is a step in the right direction. In the interim, Kirk Cousins can take a beating while the line tries to pull itself together.

I think this unit takes a step forward, but not enough to make the playoffs this year.

32. Cleveland Browns – 2025 Preseason Ranking: 17

Projected Starting Lineup

LT Spencer Fano * / Dawand Jones

LG Zion Johnson $

C Elgton Jenkins $ / Parker Brailsford *

RG Teven Jenkins

RT Tytus Howard $ / Austin Barber *

Talk about a new look. Cleveland returns no preseason projected starters from last season, after investing money and picks in its offensive line. Three stalwarts (Joel Bitonio, Jack Conklin, and Ethan Pocic) are gone, and new head coach Todd Monken is tasked with rebuilding the offense from the ground up.

RG Teven Jenkins returns for another year after starting four of the final five games in 2025. He was surprisingly good in the run game, and will have to be again for Monken. Big Dawand Jones also returns but has been relegated to a backup role heading into the season.

Starting with the new vets, Cleveland traded for Tytus Howard and signed Zion Johnson and Elgton Jenkins in free agency. None of the three are particularly good run blockers, so we’ll have to wait and see how Monken adjusts his attack.

text:
CLEVELAND, OHIO (TheOBR.com) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!

Part of the challenge with getting up at 5:30AM and sitting down to write a column is this: brain fog. You know how your eyes feel heavy, and your brain isn't firing on all cylinders? That's me, every morning when I sit down to write this Massive Morning Missive. One's fingers on the keyboard feel like clubs and tend to hit the wrong keys. Maybe that's why they tend to be a bit, as the French would say, "Le Stupide".

Fortunately for me, things actually worked out pretty well for me this morning, as there was some news - some of it actually somewhat artificial - to write about. Let's dig into the happenings of the last 24 hours.

INSURANCE HOOPLA: You know it's July when insurance, that most exciting of all financial concepts, leads the Newswire. But it does. Things started off promisingly enough yesterday morning, with PFT reporting that NFLPA records show more than $88 million in Browns cap credits tied to Deshaun Watson's injuries, thanks to insurance. That's a lot of cap clams. It's also, apparently, erroneous. While the aggregators and one fact-averse local radio station busied themselves repeating Florio's story, Over the Cap and the OBR's Jack Duffin quickly responded, saying that his calculations were wrong and that they reflected revised prorated bonus amounts rather than cap savings. The actual insurance savings still really aren't known yet, as Jack explains in Rumor Central.

So, bad information got into the system. It's what happens when dozens of sites base their business models on the concept of swiping, rephrasing, and adding a paragraph or two to someone else's work without investing in serious original efforts. Here, we don't aggregate someone else's news unless it's really big (like a Schefter trade tweet) or if we feel like we have something to add to it. There's no site that's free from referencing other sites and pages (it's part of why the web is built the way it is), but blindly repeating someone else's work is always risky, as they learned yesterday. As aggregators increasingly rely on AI for speed and lower costs, the problem will only get worse.

The bad news, of course, is that insurance help, in whatever amount it eventually turns out to be, with Watson's cap numbers won't make a huge difference for the Browns. The team still has Watson on their roster, still owes him guaranteed money, and is still trying to convince themselves that he'll find himself again six years after his last good season. The good news is that 2027 is coming, Watson won't be here for it, and the Browns will be well-positioned with financial and draft assets to use to try to finally land a quarterback who can help them win some games. It's only been forty years since the last one (apologies to Baker Mayfield), so we're right on schedule.

Insurance, it turns out, can soften the accounting bruise for a self-inflicted punch to the face of a horrible contract. To a degree. But it cannot hand the Browns a quarterback, repair seasons of roster opportunity cost, or make any of us feel smarter for having learned this much about prorated bonus credits before breakfast.

WILL RUNNING BACKS BE PRIZED AGAIN? It's been a rough go for running backs in the NFL, as the league's pass-happy ownership and Rules Committee have twisted football into being more or an aerial, high-scoring, TV-friendly game in recent decades. In this environment, the coat of quarterbacks and wide receivers has skyrocketed, whereas few teams put as much effort into their running back room. Big contracts for running backs are the exception rather than the rule, with the position sliding slowly down draft boards for years.

But that may be changing. As Jeremy Forlwer of ESPN recently reported, an AFC executive told him that WR prices have become so ridiculous that finding running backs with pass-catching talent may be a better value. We've already seen the explosion of tight ends like Harold Fannin, Jr becoming NFL stars, and pass-catching running backs could be the next big thing. Teams, the executive told Fowler, are "warming up to the fact you can get a super talented back with pass-catching ability instead."

The good news for the Browns is that they're pretty well set in this department without needing to make lavish investments. The selections of Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson in the 2025 Draft gave the Browns two backs capable of making plays out of the backfield if the Browns can finally get a quarterback who opens up defenses enough to stop line-stacking and create some uncertainty for opposing defenses.

Have a good one! GO BROWNS!

The starred Lift item this morning is a tidy little Swiss reminder that sometimes the useful answer is hiding in the space everybody else steps over. GoodGoodGood reports that Swiss startup Sun-Ways installed 48 removable solar panels along a 330-foot stretch of active railway in Buttes, Switzerland, turning the empty space between the rails into a working solar plant.

This was not a "look at our cute rendering" deal, either. More than 11,000 trains have rolled over the panels at speeds up to 55 mph, and the installation has remained stable, safe, and productive. Since May 2025, the test stretch has produced more than 16,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity — enough for the average annual consumption of three to four Swiss households — even after a snow-and-maintenance pause.

"We have achieved our objectives, both in terms of railway safety and electricity production," Sun-Ways founder Joseph Scuderi told Swissinfo. The Buttes pilot is scheduled to run through 2028, but the larger idea is the fun part: Switzerland's roughly 3,300-mile rail network could, in theory, produce up to 2% of the country's electricity, enough to power about 300,000 households.

I like this story because it is clever without being loud. No new land. No trees ripped out. No giant techno-utopian TED Talk fog machine. Just, "Hey, what if the dead space between the tracks did something useful?" Around here, after years of Browns quarterback discourse, I am emotionally prepared to support any plan that turns empty space into productive output.

title: How Will Cody Mauch's Return From Injury In 2026 Shape His Bucs Future? - Pewter Report

The countdown to the Bucs’ 2026 season is on.
Today, the series continues with right guard Cody Mauch.
26 For ‘26: Cody Mauch Bucs Storylines In 2026 How Will Cody Mauch Fare In His Return From Knee Surgery?
In A Contract Year, Cody Mauch Will Be Shaping His Future With The Bucs – Or Elsewhere?
How Mauch’s return from injury goes and whether he continues the trajectory he was on prior to his injury will directly impact the big man’s future.
text:
The countdown to the Bucs’ 2026 season is on. Right now, we’re:

68 days away from Bucs regular season kickoff

38 days away from Bucs preseason kickoff

22 days away from Bucs training camp

In the lead-up to training camp, Pewter Report’s Bailey Adams will be diving into storylines for 26 key figures who will be crucial to the Bucs’ success in 2026.

Today, the series continues with right guard Cody Mauch.

26 For ‘26: Cody Mauch Bucs Storylines In 2026

How Will Cody Mauch Fare In His Return From Knee Surgery?

When Mauch returns to game action in the preseason, it will have been 11 months since the last time he took the field in a competitive setting. Of course, when the Bucs open up the real season in Cincinnati on Sept. 13, it will have been nearly a full year since the Bucs’ right guard has played in a regular season game. His last one came on Sept. 15, 2025.

So naturally, the conversations surrounding Mauch in 2026 center on how well he’ll bounce back from the season-ending meniscus tear he suffered in Week 2 of the 2025 season. He played every snap that night, gutting it out as the Bucs came back to win late. But that was the final game he would play in his third NFL season.

Mauch missed the final 15 games of a disappointing season for Tampa Bay, and more injuries at guard led to quite the revolving door for the position throughout the campaign. But fast forward to now and the 6-foot-6, 320-pound mauler is healthy and ready to go for Year 4.

In fact, Mauch was already a full participant in practice by the start of OTAs in late May. Mauch told the media upon his return to practice that the injury was tough on him considering he hadn’t missed a snap due to injury in high school, college or the NFL. So, being sidelined was new. And it couldn’t have been easy for him to watch what unfolded for the Buccaneer offensive line and the team as a whole. The good news for him and the Bucs is that he’s now back.

But what will his return look like? Will there be a reacclimation period for Mauch? Will he be able to clear those early hurdles and shake off that rust in training camp, joint practices and the preseason? Or will there be some bumps along the way early in the regular season? The slate to start the year is unforgiving, with a pretty formidable trio of Dexter Lawrence II, Mason Graham and Javon Hargrave on the schedule within the first four weeks. The hope is that he hits the ground running right away, but time will tell for the 27-year-old.

Can Cody Mauch Stay On The Trajectory He Was On Pre-Injury?

Before the injury, Mauch was on quite the trajectory. The 2023 second-round pick took his lumps as a rookie, but that was to be expected considering he was moving from tackle to guard, the left side to the right side and North Dakota State to the NFL. There’s a learning curve and an adjustment period with all three of those transitions, and he was dealing with all three at once. He was also doing so while playing next to right tackle Luke Goedeke, who was readjusting in his own right after spending his 2022 rookie season at guard before returning to his natural college position of tackle.

In 2023, Mauch played all 1,103 of the Bucs’ offensive snaps and posted a 43.9 overall PFF grade with a 37.6 run blocking grade and a 52.1 pass blocking mark. He allowed eight sacks and 57 total pressures while being penalized five times. So, yes, there were some tough moments.

But in 2024, Mauch took a huge step up. He played 1,133 snaps for the Bucs, which came out to 99% of the offense’s total. And his grades massively improved across the board. He earned a 74.6 overall grade with a 68.4 run blocking mark and a 77.2 pass blocking grade. Mauch also allowed two sacks and 19 total pressures, which meant a quarter of the sacks he allowed in 2023 and around one-third of the pressures. He also went from five penalties in 2023 to just two in 2024. Overall, it was quite the jump from rookie season to Year 2 for Tampa Bay’s right guard.

After an injury-shortened 2025 season, Mauch and the Bucs will hope to see that rise continue in 2026. Getting through the early hurdles of his return from that meniscus tear and the ensuing surgery will be key, both mentally and physically. The physical aspect of it includes the fact that he’s carrying more weight heading into the new season, and he’s carrying that weight on a surgically repaired knee. Mauch is looking to be bigger and better in his fourth season as a pro, as he told Pewter Report.

In an April appearance on the Pewter Report Podcast, Mauch told Scott Reynolds and Matt Matera that he was weighing in the range of 320-325 pounds and was going to see how 325 pounds felt for him during OTAs. That’s about 10 more pounds than he was weighing heading into 2025, and it’s nearly 25 more than he weighed when he was drafted. It’ll be interesting to see how he manages that weight and if/how it affects his play style.

Mauch said as a guard, he thinks the bigger, the better. However he gets there, hitting an even higher level than the one he played at in 2024 would be huge for him, the offensive line and the Buccaneer offense as a whole.

In A Contract Year, Cody Mauch Will Be Shaping His Future With The Bucs – Or Elsewhere?

How Mauch’s return from injury goes and whether he continues the trajectory he was on prior to his injury will directly impact the big man’s future. Whether that future is with the Bucs or elsewhere remains to be seen, and that’s a different part of the conversation that we’ll get to shortly. Before that, let’s focus on the fact that 2026 is a contract year for Mauch, making it a massively important season for him.

The timing of Mauch’s meniscus injury creates a unique situation for him in 2026. Because as much as this season will be about finishing up his recovery, readjusting to the grind of the NFL season, returning to form and even taking the next step after a hugely successful 2024 season, it’s also about him establishing his value as he’s set to hit free agency.

As of May, Pewter Report’s Josh Queipo projected Mauch to make between $14 million-$17 million per year on a new contract. This season will help determine whether the average annual value (AAV) on his new contract will be on the lower end of that range, the higher end or even beyond that $17 million. This season could also play a role in deciding whether Mauch’s future is with the Bucs or one of the 31 other teams in the league. And that’s an interesting layer of this conversation.

Right now, it would feel like a big surprise – and potentially a big misstep – for Tampa Bay to pass on re-signing Mauch. He’s just now hitting his prime heading into his age-27 season, and he was on the right path prior to the injury that ended his 2025. Assuming he returns to the field fully healthy and has another very good season for the Bucs, Mauch very well could and should be a priority next offseason.

But there’s a lot that the Bucs have to juggle next offseason. Baker Mayfield, Yaya Diaby, Vita Vea and Chase McLaughlin are all pending free agents. And there’s only so much cash to go around, right? Well, as Queipo suggested back in that May article, there’s a chance a decision has to be made between re-signing Mauch and retaining Ben Bredeson for the third and final year of his three-year contract. In that situation, you’re choosing Bredeson to be a cap casualty and Mauch to be a long-term building block for the offensive line 100/100 times.

In any case, Mauch is set to play out his contract year unless Tampa Bay inks him to an early extension in the coming weeks. There hasn’t been any smoke on that, though, so this may be a topic that’s tabled until next February or March. But it’s a topic that will linger as a critical thread throughout the upcoming season.

text:
AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — Former Dallas Cowboys defensive end Marshawn Kneeland, who died by suicide in November 2025 after a high-speed chase with police, had early stage chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, a brain abnormality linked to repeated concussions, his family announced Tuesday.

The Boston University CTE Center, which investigates the long-term consequences of repetitive brain trauma in athletes and others, analyzed Kneeland's brain tissue after his death. Researchers determined Kneeland, who was 24, was in stage one of four of CTE.

EDITOR’S NOTE — This story includes discussion of suicide. If you or someone you know needs help, the National Suicide and Crisis Lifeline in the U.S. is available by calling or texting 988. There is also an online chat at 988lifeline.org

CTE is a degenerative brain disease that has been found in athletes in contact sports, combat veterans and others who experience repetitive head trauma. It has been known to cause violent mood swings, impulsive behavior and depression. It can be diagnosed only after death.

“While this diagnosis does not change the tragedy of his passing, it provides important context about some of the struggles he may have been facing. We share this information to help people understand what NFL and other high contact sport athletes might be struggling with,” Kneeland’s family, including his girlfriend, Catalina Mancera, said in a statement issued through the Concussion and CTE Foundation.

“Raising awareness is important to us. We continue to remember Marshawn with compassion for the person he was, rather than defining him by the final moments of his life. One Love,” the family said.

The abnormality has also been linked to deaths in the National Football League, as well as in hockey and soccer.

Kneeland shot himself after evading authorities in his vehicle and fleeing a car crash on foot.

The chase happened after police said Kneeland didn’t stop for Texas Department of Public Safety troopers over a traffic violation. Authorities lost sight of the vehicle before locating it crashed minutes later.

As authorities were looking for Kneeland after he fled the crash site on foot, a dispatcher told officers that people who knew him had received a group text from Kneeland “saying goodbye,” indicating he might be suicidal.

According to a 2021 study by the Harvard Medical School and the Boston University CTE Center, NFL players are more than four times more likely to develop ALS than other men.

Dr. Chris Nowinski, CEO of the Concussion & CTE Foundation, noted Kneeland's diagnosis comes even amid a modern era of concussion protocols in professional and college athletics and better safety equipment.

Kneeland started playing tackle football when he was 7 years old. He played at Western Michigan University before he was selected by the Cowboys in the second round of the 2024 NFL draft.

“We have no reason to believe the current generation is at a lower risk of CTE than previous generations. Concussion protocols do not prevent CTE, because CTE is caused by repeated head impacts, not just concussions,” Nowinski said. “If we want to reduce CTE risk, we must implement CTE prevention protocols and aggressively reduce the number and strength of head impacts at every level of the game.”

title: Can the NY Giants upgraded offensive line make up for Malik Nabers' injury?
description:
Still, the biggest offensive upgrades this offseason have been to the offensive line.
It’s honestly kinda weird that people still cite the Giants’ offensive line as a problem.
I wouldn’t go so far as to say that the Giants’ offensive line was a weapon against defenses, but it was certainly a “quality” unit.
Fielding a top-5 running game that’s only supplemented — not driven — by the quarterback will be a big unlock for this team.
Has the Giants’ offensive line been upgraded enough to win even when the numbers aren’t in their favor?
text:
There is a definite sense of optimism surrounding the New York Giants, and real excitement for what the team can be in 2026.

The Giants are considered one of the most likely teams in the NFL to make the leap from worst to first and could challenge the Philadelphia Eagles for the division crown. The biggest reason for that is the arrival of head coach John Harbaugh, but the Giants have also had a strong off-season that may have brought upgrades to almost every position on the field.

The first priority for the Giants this off-season has been to build an environment in which Jaxson Dart can mature into a true franchise quarterback. ESPN polled their NFC East writers on the state of the teams they cover, and the very first question was how each team’s off-season impacts their respective quarterback.

Giants writer Jordan Raanan noted the Giants’ many additions to their skill positions as a potential improvement for Dart, but believes the (potential) improvements to the offensive line will have a bigger impact.

The Giants have contingencies for Jaxson Dart with the signings of tight end Isaiah Likely and wide receivers Darnell Mooney, Calvin Austin III and even Odell Beckham Jr. Of course, it would also be nice if he had star wide receiver Malik Nabers at his disposal. Nabers is still recovering from a serious knee injury and remains uncertain for Week 1, although the Giants remain hopeful.

It would be a bit more than “nice” if the Giants have Nabers for the start of the 2026 season. That said, the Giants have certainly done a good job of giving themselves options when it comes to pass catchers. Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney will probably be quality additions to the offense, with the potential to be much more. Calvin Austin III has the potential to be an explosive weapon, while Beckham and Smith-Schuster could become reliable options for Dart.

There’s the potential for high variance with all these players, and they’re all more likely to hit their positive outcomes with Nabers on the field.

If Nabers isn’t ready to start the year, Raanan believes that the additions of Sisi Mauigoa and Patrick Ricard will help smooth things out while Nabers finds his way back to the field and rounds into form.

Still, the biggest offensive upgrades this offseason have been to the offensive line. Shhhh, don’t tell anyone. The Giants’ offensive line isn’t just fixed, it’s the strength of the offense after the additions of right guard Francis Mauigoa with the 10th draft pick and the signing of All-Pro fullback Patrick Ricard. The biggest thing Dart has going for him is that he should have the help of quality protection and a running game.

It’s honestly kinda weird that people still cite the Giants’ offensive line as a problem. I get it: Narratives go around the world while facts are still tying their shoes. But still, the Giants finished 11th in pass protection and 18th in run blocking. And that’s with Andrew Thomas (4 games), Jon Runyan Jr. (1 game), John Michael Schmitz (4 games), and Jermaine Eluemunor (1 game) all missing time last year. I wouldn’t go so far as to say that the Giants’ offensive line was a weapon against defenses, but it was certainly a “quality” unit.

Dart certainly wasn’t running for his life and was his own worst enemy when it came to protection at times

It will be interesting to see how the Giants’ running game changes with the new regime, as well as Mauigoa and Ricard. The Giants were 5th in rushing yards per game, rushing touchdowns, and rushing EPA last year, so it’s also not like that was lagging in any regard. That said, we do need to see the load shift from Jaxson Dart to the running backs.

Dart is one of the best running quarterbacks in the NFL, and legitimately runs like a running back. His vision and agility make his legs a weapon, but it should be a weapon of last resort. Fielding a top-5 running game that’s only supplemented — not driven — by the quarterback will be a big unlock for this team.

Turning back to Nabers, his status is a big concern for the Giants for a couple reasons. First and foremost, while the Giants have added a bunch of new pass catchers to their offense, Nabers’ presence what would allow them to play their “natural” roles.

He’s still the one elite player on the Giants’ offense. They need him healthy, and he’s already uncertain for the start of the season. It’s not exactly overly encouraging that Nabers was injured in Week 4 and isn’t a lock to be ready almost 11 months later. He had his right ACL and meniscus repaired and required a second surgery earlier this year to remove scar tissue. The Giants have their fingers crossed with their No. 1 receiver.

And even when he does come back, can they really expect him to be back to being a Pro Bowl-caliber player immediately? The whole situation is definitely concerning.

Perhaps Darnell Mooney or Darius Slayton could step up, or perhaps Odell Beckham Jr. or JuJu Smith-Schuster could turn back the clock if Nabers isn’t ready to start the season. However, Nabers not being a threat all over the field and forcing the defense scheme for him will be tough to replicate or scheme around for the Giants.

The other concern is whether the Giants can force defenses to respect their passing game without (or with a diminished) Nabers. We’ve mentioned this several times before, but it’s really the proliferation of split-field coverages (Cover 2 and Cover 4) that has driven the resurgence of the run game. Two deep safeties all but guarantees that offenses will see neutral or light boxes, which gives the offense the numbers advantage.

The hope is that the Giants will be able to lean on their run game to take the pressure off of Dart and the Giants’ pass catchers without Nabers. But will they be able to run like they want to if defenses don’t feel forced to play two-deep coverages?

Has the Giants’ offensive line been upgraded enough to win even when the numbers aren’t in their favor? And can the legion of new pass catchers make defenses pay for disrespecting them?

We’ll find out soon enough, but that has to be the single biggest question about the Giants as training camp approaches.

title: What's next for Brady Christensen? Longtime Panthers lineman dishes on future - Charlotte Observer
description:
